CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Increased nuchal translucency >4mm detected at <14 weeks gestation with elevated screening risk for chromosomal abnormalities.

SPECIMEN TYPE
Chorionic villus sample obtained at 14 weeks gestation

TEST PERFORMED
1. Rapid PCR analysis of uncultured chorionic villi for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
2. Targeted G-banded chromosome analysis focusing on chromosome 21

METHODOLOGY
Rapid PCR: Quantitative fluorescence PCR (QF-PCR) was performed on uncultured chorionic villi using STR markers specific for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. DNA was extracted using standard protocols and amplified with fluorescent primers.

Karyotype Analysis: Following rapid PCR results, targeted G-banded analysis was performed on cultured chorionic villi cells. A minimum of 15 metaphases were analyzed with specific attention to chromosome 21. Banding resolution was at least 400 bands per haploid set.

RESULTS

RAPID PCR RESULTS:
Chromosome 21: TRISOMY DETECTED
Three distinct alleles identified for D21S1411 and D21S1435 markers
Chromosome 13: Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 18: Normal disomic pattern
Sex chromosomes: XY (male)

KARYOTYPE RESULTS:
47,XY,+21

ABNORMAL MALE KARYOTYPE WITH TRISOMY 21

All cells examined showed three copies of chromosome 21, consistent with primary trisomy 21. No mosaicism detected in the cells analyzed.

INTERPRETATION
The cytogenetic findings demonstrate primary trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this male fetus. The presence of three copies of chromosome 21 in all cells examined indicates a non-mosaic form of Down syndrome. This abnormality most likely resulted from a spontaneous meiotic nondisjunction event during gametogenesis or less commonly from a post-zygotic mitotic error.

The karyotype findings are consistent with the ultrasound observation of increased nuchal translucency and the elevated screening risk. Individuals with trisomy 21 have characteristic facial features, intellectual disability of varying degrees, and increased risk for congenital heart defects, gastrointestinal abnormalities, and other medical conditions.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
2. Parental karyotyping is not indicated as primary trisomy 21 is typically a de novo event
3. The recurrence risk for trisomy 21 in future pregnancies is slightly elevated above the maternal age-related risk
4. For future pregnancies, we recommend:
   - First trimester combined screening (biochemical markers and ultrasound)
   - Detailed ultrasound monitoring
   - Consideration of prenatal diagnosis via chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis

This report has been reviewed and electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
Board Certified Clinical Cytogeneticist
